title: Azure Functions from C#
description: Create HTTP-triggered and timer-triggered Azure Functions in C# with the isolated worker model.

data.text: In the isolated worker model, every function is a method on a class decorated with a [Function] attribute. The method signature declares its trigger and any bindings, and the DI container provides services like ILogger and IHostEnvironment.

data.title: Program.cs — register Functions worker and services

data.text: An HTTP-triggered function is the serverless equivalent of a minimal API endpoint. You control the response type, status code, and body directly from C#.

data.title: WeatherFunction.cs — HTTP-triggered GET endpoint

data.text: Timer triggers use a CRON expression to run on a schedule. The TimerInfo parameter gives you access to schedule status and last run details.

data.title: CleanupFunction.cs — timer-triggered scheduled job
Always handle CancellationToken
data.text: Azure Functions pass a CancellationToken to every invocation. Respect it in async operations so Azure can gracefully shut down your function during scale-in or deployment events.

data.title: Build an HTTP-triggered health-check function
data.description: Create a new Functions project and add an HTTP-triggered function that returns a JSON health status object.
steps: Create a new isolated-worker Functions project with dotnet new worker
Return a JSON object with status "Healthy", the UTC timestamp, and the environment name
Register any needed services in Program.cs
data.expectedOutcome: GET /api/health-check returns 200 with { status: "Healthy", timestamp: "2026-01-15T...", environment: "Development" }

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use the isolated worker model for new Functions projects
Decorate methods with [Function] and a trigger attribute (HttpTrigger, TimerTrigger)
Inject ILogger<T> and other services via constructor DI
Always accept and respect CancellationToken in async function code
Return HttpResponseData for HTTP triggers; re-throw on timer failures
data.takeaway: The isolated worker model gives Azure Functions the same clean architecture patterns you already use in ASP.NET Core.
